harbor_p15_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_001.text: The seventeenth week began with a merchant's sample parcel placed in the middle of He Ming's table. It was beautifully wrapped, too beautifully for the price the merchant proposed. Zhou Yin turned it over and found three unnecessary folds. An Shou said the buyer wanted a parcel that looked expensive while paying for one that looked hurried. He Ming almost accepted the challenge as a compliment. Then she counted the minutes required to imitate it. A useful new business could disappear inside the pleasure of proving its workers clever, and she had already spent enough pride on spoiled paper.

harbor_p15_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_002.text: Miao had brought the sample for a cloth trader who needed a modest shore batch. His own voyage agency work continued separately, under revised waiting terms and ordinary merchant payments. He put the proposed packing price beside the sample and admitted the trader had imagined fewer steps. Zhou asked whether his fee depended on forcing their price down. It did not; he had a fixed introduction fee from the trader, disclosed in the offer. She still watched his face while he answered. A clear term made suspicion less convenient. It did not make her forget his earlier conflicting dispatch instruction.

harbor_p15_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_003.text: The partners made a alternative parcel using sound stock and the maker's cord limit. It protected the cloth under the actual storage and handling conditions without pretending to be an ornate gift. Miao carried it to the trader and returned with a revised proposal. Forty-eight copper would cover the bounded batch. Materials would cost twelve, work space six and wages thirty. The contract required four workers at different hours, not four equal shares. He Ming, Zhou and An would receive eight each; Wu would receive six for two scheduled half-days. The three partners discussed it before offering anything to her.

harbor_p15_004.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p15_004.text: We have actual demand this time, and the two half-days match the hours Wu said might suit. She can refuse without losing the canteen friendship or the lesson she already took. We should tell her the work is this batch, with its payment date and what she will do. I do not want to call it joining our family. Families can be wonderful at asking people to work for free. If she likes the method afterward, we can discuss another offer when another buyer exists. The table has four places; it does not have four promises.

harbor_p15_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_005.text: Wu read the offer after her canteen shift with the duck basket under the bench. She asked whether the first half-day could begin an hour later because the children needed taking to their neighbor's supervised room. The partners checked the actual sequence and agreed. She would receive three copper per half-day, six after the agreed completion check. Her canteen supervisor approved the ordinary availability change; she kept that dependable job. Wu laughed when He Ming said she could still refuse. She said she understood, and wanted the work. The answer felt different from being told she was welcome everywhere.

harbor_p15_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_006.text: The trader paid the agreed twenty-four advance. Twelve bought materials, six paid the booked work space, and six made initial wage payments of two to each original partner. The remaining twenty-four would pay the last eighteen of their wages and Wu's six after completion. No surplus was assumed, and the partners accepted that the price bought a bounded job rather than a permanent reserve. Zhou wanted the next quote to include replacement stock and a margin. An wanted proof they could finish this batch first. He Ming wrote both concerns in their private notebook beside the actual advance receipt.

harbor_p15_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_007.text: Yue visited on her free afternoon and was assigned the honorable task of staying outside the production lane with her tea. Wu said visitors always wanted to improve work by standing where parcels had to pass. He Ming agreed so quickly that Yue felt accused. She found a seat by the window and watched the four workers settle into their different motions. Zhou folded sharply, An tied neatly, Wu checked the finished surface with the concentration of a person learning where speed belonged. He Ming corrected one corner by asking, not by taking the parcel out of Wu's hands.

harbor_p15_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_008.text: A child from the neighboring room appeared at the doorway asking whether the duck could enter the workforce. Wu said its attendance was poor and its opinions too loud. An suggested it supervise the merchant. Zhou said the merchant might already be a duck in better clothes. He Ming tried to keep a professional face because Miao was approaching with the delivery check, and failed. The agent heard the end of the conversation and said he had once been bitten by a goose. Nobody knew how this defended merchants, but the child found the qualification persuasive.

harbor_p15_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_009.text: The batch's first mistake belonged to He Ming. She had set aside the wrong color tie for a group whose buyer specified a identifying mark. Wu noticed before the parcels closed and hesitated to interrupt. He Ming saw the hesitation and asked what she had found. The correction cost a few minutes and saved a later return. Zhou looked pleased in a way He Ming did not enjoy. Afterward she thanked Wu directly. She wanted her new worker to speak next time without needing to examine the founder's pride first. Founding a table had made pride alarmingly easy to bruise.

harbor_p15_010.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p15_010.text: I was wrong about that group. The mark matters because the receiver has to separate them, and you saw it before I did. Please say it as soon as you see it next time. You do not need to wait until I look agreeable. Zhou has been waiting for me to look agreeable for years and has almost no evidence that the method works. We can all stop a parcel for the agreed check. We can also stop for lunch. An, if you tie another knot while I am saying lunch, I will make you eat the knot.

harbor_p15_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_011.text: An put down the cord and said the knot would have more flavor than the canteen's last turnip. Wu accused him of slandering an honorable vegetable. They ate from bowls each had arranged through ordinary private purchases. Yue joined by invitation, still seated outside the work lane. The talk turned to prices, then weather, then a neighbor's wedding where somebody had mistaken salt for sugar in a cake. He Ming laughed until her eyes watered. For a quarter-hour her partnership was simply people eating together before work, with no need to demonstrate that it would save anybody's life.

harbor_p15_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_012.text: He Jun's next letter arrived that evening. Their mother needed a warmer quilt and preferred choosing it from the Willow Reach seller she knew. Jun could pay part from his repair wages. He asked whether He Ming wanted to contribute a stated amount, not send a quilt she had selected from a harbor shop. She counted the available money from her completed contracts and chose a contribution she could spare without borrowing from the advance. The quilt would belong to their mother. He Ming wrote this solemnly that Jun would later tease her about giving property advice to a blanket.

harbor_p15_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_013.text: Zhou asked why she looked disappointed after making a sensible arrangement. He Ming said she had imagined carrying the quilt inland herself and being told the harbor had made her prosperous. Now her mother would buy a familiar quilt and thank two children she had never considered failures anyway. An said this was terrible treatment of a woman's ambition. The joke made He Ming laugh and then confess the rest: she had wanted her mother to need the new business. Zhou said she needed the business because she liked the work. That was a less grand and more durable reason.

harbor_p15_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_014.text: At the canteen, Wu's neighbor explained that he could cover the children's room for the two agreed afternoons but not become their permanent keeper whenever packing work expanded. Wu accepted the limit and thanked him with a privately bought portion of the fish he liked. Her children wanted to know whether more packing money meant a bigger room. She said it meant six copper from this job, which could buy several useful things but had no authority to stretch walls. The older child suggested fewer duck feathers would help. The duck shook itself at precisely the wrong moment.

harbor_p15_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_015.text: The room's landlord asked whether Wu intended to sublet the outer bench for packing storage. She did not. The children had carried sample wrapping home, and a neighbor assumed commercial work had moved in. Wu showed what was there and asked that future questions come to her directly. The landlord agreed, embarrassed by the rumor. He Ming heard the story afterward and offered to keep all future sample material at the work room. Wu said she could still bring a harmless scrap home if her children wanted it. Friendship did not require turning an ordinary toy into a permit application.

harbor_p15_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_016.text: Fen helped the children make a paper gull from that scrap. It looked more like a bent turnip, which delighted Wu. Aning said turnips were underrated birds. The younger child made it chase the toy boat across the floor until the duck attempted to eat its wing. Yue watched from the doorway with a bowl the household had invited her to share. She remembered arriving alone at this harbor and knowing none of these objects. Now their cheap, battered forms had histories she could follow. None needed to enter her pack to remain part of her life.

harbor_p15_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_017.text: Miao's merchant employer sent a voyage offer while the packing batch proceeded. The agent could earn another bonus if claims against the upcoming voyage guarantee remained below a threshold. Its wording differed from the earlier lost twenty, but it felt familiar. He read it at the tea stall, where nobody knew what decision the paper asked of him. He had already revised waiting terms once. He could accept this new incentive and tell himself he would still act fairly. The paper did not command him to conceal a claim. It made concealment financially attractive, which was enough to trouble him.

harbor_p15_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_018.text: He asked Song An's commercial office for the published agency-incentive rule and disclosed the proposed wording to the employer. The office supplied its actual scope: it could review contractual compliance and conflicts raised in a supported dispute, not dictate every private bonus. Miao then wrote his own refusal of that particular condition and proposed a fixed fee with a timely-completion bonus that excluded withholding supported worker claims. The employer had no duty to admire him. It could decline the new arrangement. He mailed the proposal with his hands shaking and spent the evening wanting to call the letter back.

harbor_p15_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_019.text: The packing trader liked the completed sample and asked the partnership to reserve all its next month for his deliveries. The proposed exclusivity carried no guaranteed minimum quantity. An heard security in the phrase next month. Zhou heard four weeks that might produce no paid work. Wu reminded them she had promised only the present two half-days and would not give up the canteen for unspecified calls. He Ming wanted a steady buyer badly enough to dislike her own agreement with them. She asked Miao to obtain an actual minimum offer before they considered tying up their future hours.

harbor_p15_020.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p15_020.text: You brought this to me as a friend, so I will answer as one. The words next month do not look like work until somebody says how much work and what happens if none arrives. I have learned that lesson at an office desk often enough to recognize it in a merchant's handwriting. But I also know wanting a stable income can make uncertainty look like an insult. You can ask the question without announcing he is dishonest. Then you can hear the answer. If it is a refusal, that tells you something you needed to know.

harbor_p15_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_021.text: He Ming said she disliked sensible advice most when she had asked for it. Han said she charged extra for that difficulty, in imaginary copper accepted nowhere. They shared supper and discussed Jun's quilt letter. Han admitted her own family thought painting was a waste unless it became a trade. She liked the board precisely because nobody paid her to make it. He Ming asked whether she might paint the partnership's public sign. Han said a commission needed terms and a skill she did not yet possess reliably. She could offer an ugly private gull for the room instead.

harbor_p15_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_022.text: The ugly gull arrived two days later on a scrap board Han bought with her own money and gave by choice. It was worse than the gull at home because she had tried to make it distinguished. Zhou hung it above the lunch shelf and called it the superintendent. An claimed its left eye disapproved of his knots. Wu said its right eye disapproved of everyone's wage. He Ming loved it too much to say so comfortably. The sign announcing their work remained the plain existing one. A friend's gift could be cherished without pretending it certified a business.

harbor_p15_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_023.text: Yue saw the gull during a permitted social visit and asked whether its cultivation realm was known. Han, who had come for tea, said its stage was permanently embarrassed. The joke made Yue laugh more loudly than expected. People nearby glanced over, and she felt self-conscious about how rare that laugh had become in public rooms. He Ming refilled her cup and resumed an argument about the trader's offer. The conversation allowed Yue to be a person at a table instead of the visitor whose every reaction had to carry a lesson. She stayed until the kettle emptied.

harbor_p15_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_024.text: The trader's revised offer guaranteed one modest minimum batch, but still asked them to refuse all competing buyers. Zhou calculated the lost freedom against that limited guarantee. An thought the buyer might bring more work once trusted. He Ming asked whether trust required every risk to lie on their side. The partners agreed to offer a narrower reserved window for the guaranteed batch and keep other hours open. Miao delivered the counteroffer. The trader declined, citing his own uncertain cargo schedule. Their sensible boundary cost them the comforting prospect of a month with one name above it.

harbor_p15_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_025.text: An left the room before the discussion ended. He had rent due and believed Zhou could afford principles more easily because she shared a household with her sister. Zhou followed him into the yard and said her sister's wages were not their business reserve. They argued where Yue could hear but did not invite her to arbitrate. He Ming stayed inside staring at the ugly gull. A cooperative could have prices and still contain different levels of fear. Equal voices did not give those voices equal cushions beneath them. She had not imagined this when she first wanted a table.

harbor_p15_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_026.text: The next morning An returned with a proposal for an ordinary smaller job he had found through his own contacts. It would fill part of the lost window without exclusivity, though the price needed checking. Zhou apologized for dismissing his rent worry as impatience. An apologized for treating her sister's home as proof that she could not understand. They made no grand vow never to quarrel again. The work would need separate agreement and actual receipts. He Ming put the proposal beside the first batch's remaining tasks. The table had survived its first serious argument with all three chairs occupied.

harbor_p15_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_027.text: Wu completed her second half-day after the children left for the supervised room. She knew the checking rhythm now and stopped one parcel where the outer fold covered the mark. The trader's receiver accepted the finished batch under the agreed conditions. Twenty-four balance copper arrived. Eighteen completed the partners' wages at eight each in total, and six paid Wu's two half-days. The forty-eight contract closed against twelve materials, six space and thirty wages. There was no leftover fund to finance the rejected month. Wu counted her own six carefully, then put half aside for the children's next ordinary expense.

harbor_p15_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_028.text: The receiver said the partnership ought to accept the trader's exclusive offer after all because the work was good. Zhou asked whether good work made guaranteed pay less necessary. He smiled as if she had made a clever joke and did not answer. Miao, beside him, repeated the actual counteroffer rather than soften it into willingness. He Ming noticed. The agent had not become their friend by failing to charm the trader. He had performed the introduction honestly after a history that gave them reason to watch him. That was a change she could acknowledge without making a larger promise.

harbor_p15_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_029.text: Miao's employer rejected his alternative bonus proposal and offered him fewer voyages at a fixed rate instead. It was lawful under the term and disappointing. He could ask advice about the next contract, but no public office owed him his imagined income. He told Yue at the stall because he wanted somebody to recognize the cost of his decision. She said she did. Then she asked whether he wanted company or an opinion. He chose company. They ate ordinary bowls in silence while a neighboring customer complained about fish prices, a subject indifferent to either man's or woman's moral courage.

harbor_p15_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_030.text: After supper Miao said he had once imagined leaving agency work to sell ordinary tools. Every time a contract disappointed him, he made the fantasy shop a little better stocked. Yue asked what tools he knew how to judge. He admitted very few. They laughed, and the laugh hurt him less than he expected. A future could be considered without becoming an escape hatch from the consequences already pending. He would still attend the commercial review's next hearing about the improper transfer. Tonight he bought a pencil with his own money and wrote down what a real shop would require.

harbor_p15_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_031.text: Fen took the account shop's trial sheet to Han for an arithmetic question. The clerk explained one example during a private break, then asked Fen to work the next herself. Fen wanted the answer quickly enough to nearly copy the first pattern without checking the numbers. Han caught the mistake and showed where it changed. The girl groaned, embarrassed. Han said painting had taught her what happened when a hand expected praise before finishing a line. Fen looked at her inked fingers and asked whether letters were less troublesome than numbers. Han said they were troublesome in longer sentences.

harbor_p15_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_032.text: Luo waited outside with a basket he had bought cheaply for paper sorting. His care review had permitted its light use; he was not returning to heavy bundles. Fen came out smiling over the solved example and asked whether he wanted to see. He said yes, then asked when she would decide about the trial. She told him the following week. He nodded without adding the warning he had prepared. On the way home she asked why he was quiet. He said he was trying to learn a new kind of company, where he walked beside her instead of ahead.

harbor_p15_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_033.text: The sentence pleased Fen and made her sad. She had wanted him to say it, but she had also missed being a child who could assume he knew the road. She told Aning later that independence seemed like receiving a good gift with a broken old one inside. Aning said her father's worry still occupied most of their supper table, even after the aunt's trial had begun. The two girls sat beneath the shop eaves sharing a privately purchased bun. They did not solve either household. They spoke long enough to discover each could understand the other's impossible gratitude.

harbor_p15_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_034.text: Wu used two of her new copper to buy a sturdy fastening for the room's storage chest. The children wanted a painted toy bird instead. She explained the chest would protect their clothes from the duck's experiments and promised no immediate bird. The older child examined the fastening with reluctant respect, then proposed painting it. Their landlord gave permission for an ordinary removable decoration on the tenant-owned chest, not the wall. By evening the clasp had a face. Wu laughed when He Ming visited and said this was what prosperity looked like in a house where children were permitted opinions.

harbor_p15_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_035.text: He Ming brought no advice about the other four copper. She had begun to notice how often help became an interest in somebody else's private spending. Wu made tea and asked whether the partners intended to give her another task. He Ming said An's smaller job was still only a proposal. If it became real, they would ask whether her hours fit. Wu nodded and returned to sewing a sleeve. The absence of a new offer disappointed her. It also let her plan the canteen week without waiting for an encouraging word that might never become a wage.

harbor_p15_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_036.text: At the quay, the tide returned to its familiar rhythm. Bo dared a coworker to identify the exact storm peak on a wall now drying into several confused lines. Yan interrupted the bet only because they had a check to finish, not because young people were forbidden to gamble imaginary coins. The crew had been issued the corrected waiting map after the cart obstruction review. Bo traced the old mark and shook his head. A small outdated ink stroke had taken space from a frightened woman's transfer. He understood the comparison more deeply now that he remembered her torn sleeve.

harbor_p15_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_037.text: Yan asked Bo to run the next handover while he listened. The young rigger began too quickly, skipped the tool count, then restarted when Deren coughed pointedly from the dry table. Everybody knew the cough was theatrical. Bo finished with the count and the changed lane mark, then asked whether applause was included in the wage. Deren said competent work came with competent silence. The crew laughed. Yan wrote the signoff and later told Bo what he had done well. Encouragement could be specific enough to survive the next day without becoming a declaration that the boy never erred.

harbor_p15_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_038.text: Deren worried that his dry table work would become permanent after the care review allowed more movement. He liked the crew and hated feeling he had acquired a chair because a platform had failed beneath him. The attendant said recovery would be assessed through function, not the symbolic importance of climbing again. He asked Yan about future duties after clearance, and the foreman described openings without assigning them in advance. Deren then complained about the table's wobble. A carpenter repaired it under the ordinary work-room maintenance. A present task deserved a sound table even if its worker hoped to leave.

harbor_p15_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_039.text: Ke Chun found a short canvas-sorting task at the shop she had visited. Its terms matched her current dry light-work restriction, and the shop provided its own tools. She received the ordinary agreed wage after the first completed interval. Tong accompanied her to the doorway and said he had found a similarly compatible stock task elsewhere. Their conversation remained awkward. Ke wanted him to admit the jacket mattered; he wanted her to stop repeating it. Finally he said it had mattered and he was ashamed. She answered that so had her tools. The two truths made the next silence easier.

harbor_p15_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_040.text: Ke borrowed a stitching needle from the shop only for its assigned work and returned it to the keeper when the shift ended. Outside she flexed her empty fingers and looked frustrated. Yue, passing after her own half-day, asked whether she wanted to walk to the public tool seller. Ke did, although she could not yet afford the old kit. They inspected a cheaper ordinary needle. Ke decided to buy one from her new wage rather than wait for a complete replacement award. Its price did not settle the incident claim. It gave her one usable object now.

harbor_p15_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_041.text: The seller wrapped the needle in a small stiff paper. Ke held it like a gift she had given herself reluctantly. She told Yue her late father had bought the first kit when she entered stitching work, and losing it felt like being told she had never belonged to the trade. Yue understood why a price could not explain the bag. She said the new needle did not have to imitate the old one before Ke could use it. Ke said that sounded like advice from a person who owned one cup for too long. They both laughed.

harbor_p15_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_042.text: Dai Min's net work brought an evening customer who remembered her husband and began a story she did not want to hear. The man mistook her polite silence for encouragement. Dai interrupted and asked him to describe the actual repair he needed. He apologized, then did. He Ming witnessed the exchange and admired the interruption more than any graceful response could have impressed her. Later Dai said she had been grateful for memories on another day. This day she needed to finish a knot before the light failed. Grief did not make every visitor's story a service.

harbor_p15_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_043.text: At Han's room, Yue attempted to describe the afternoon and became caught in her own habit of listing outcomes. Han asked which part had stayed in her mind. Yue said Ke's hands around the small needle. The clerk put down her brush and listened. They spoke about possessions carried through different lives, then about the rooms in which people began leaving ordinary objects behind because they expected to return. Yue's pack sat near the door. Han did not ask her to unpack permanently. She asked whether she wanted another shelf for the next few months, and Yue said yes.

harbor_p15_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_044.text: The shelf belonged to Han's rented room and stayed there. Yue placed a private notebook on it during visits, with Han's permission, and brought it away when she needed it. The arrangement felt larger than its physical size. She had been careful to acquire no harbor equipment that would follow her onward, but friendship was not equipment. It could make a departure heavier without adding a single object to the pack. Han noticed her staring and said the shelf charged no rent for philosophy. Yue answered that the board looked structurally unfit for such a load. The clerk laughed.

harbor_p15_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_045.text: Yue practiced the next morning before work on the dry training strip. Her two earned pairs formed within her familiar measured interval. She used a chalk marker set on her paper, moved it through the small agreed range and released the arms before strain made control careless. There was no new stage hidden in an emotional week. Rest showed itself as steadier familiar motion. A child watching from beyond the boundary asked whether four arms could fold four parcels at once. Yue said not responsibly in the partnership's work room, which disappointed him more than a grand limitation would have.

harbor_p15_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_046.text: He Ming heard the question and offered Yue a parcel for ordinary two-handed practice during a private visit, with no production payment or quota attached. Yue made the outer fold crooked. Wu, now a paid worker for the completed job and only a visitor today, corrected her with cheerful severity. The lesson produced no merchant goods; the practice wrapping was reused at home. Yue discovered she liked being bad at a harmless task. Nobody feared for a household when the edge bent. She could laugh, unfold it and try again without making a court file.

harbor_p15_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_047.text: The next proposal from An's contact became a paid job for the three partners only. Its schedule did not match Wu's available hours, so they told her rather than pretend four workers were needed for every future batch. The price covered the materials, space and three stated wage shares, with receipts to be closed on completion. Zhou wanted a public name for the partnership that did not imply they were a whole harbor guild. An suggested Three Chairs, then remembered Wu's first job and looked embarrassed. He Ming proposed leaving the name undecided until the work stopped changing their minds.

harbor_p15_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_048.text: Miao brought word that the large trader had found another packer willing to accept his exclusivity offer. An went quiet. He Ming felt the old desire to reverse their refusal just to avoid being replaced. Zhou asked Miao whether the new packer had a guaranteed quantity. He did not know and did not guess. The partners returned to their actual smaller job. A sound decision could still feel like losing a contest nobody had honestly offered to judge. That evening An bought one bun instead of two and said he hoped principles became edible before his next rent day.

harbor_p15_049.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p15_049.text: I will not tell you the smaller work proves we were right about everything. We chose a narrower risk, and it may still leave us short some weeks. If your rent makes that impossible, tell us before you stay silent and resent the table. We can change a price, take outside work or decide the partnership cannot carry all our hours. None of those choices means you betrayed us. I used to think a shared venture asked people to stay. Now I think it has to make leaving a possible sentence, or every promise becomes a trap.

harbor_p15_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_050.text: An said he wanted to stay for now and would take an ordinary outside shift where it fit. Zhou accepted that the table could be part of a livelihood instead of its whole foundation. He Ming disliked losing the grand picture she had carried in her head. Then she watched An tie the next sound knot and realized the smaller picture contained actual hands. Their partnership did not need to declare itself the final answer to migrant insecurity. It could pay a worker for a particular batch and leave him able to seek another wage without hiding it.

harbor_p15_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_051.text: The district employment reviewer sent Rao Tong a date for the supported comparison of his complaint. The witness had received notice under the stated privacy terms. Rao asked Han whether he should bring every old grievance against the foreman. She directed him to the reviewer for scope and helped him separate the current split-strap report from unrelated memories. He disliked the narrowness and later admitted it let him say what mattered clearly. Yue read only the public referral result during her own work. The worker's detailed statement remained at its keeper, where friendship could not turn it into an anecdote.

harbor_p15_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_052.text: The household desk's new aunt inquiry ended with a permitted reply saying the woman was well and did not wish to share her address. Her nephew arrived expecting a reunion location and left with a sentence he found cruel. Han explained the actual consent limit without pretending the woman's choice proved the nephew dangerous. He might be lonely and still have no authority to override her. Yue watched him fold the reply carefully before putting it away. Some stories ended with a road closed by somebody's preference, rather than a storm. The office's task was to preserve that answer too.

harbor_p15_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_053.text: Qin heard about the case only through the permitted general discussion of the contact method. He said his wife had once taken a week away to visit a sister without telling him every stop, and he had behaved as though marriage granted a map. The memory embarrassed him. He told it to Han over tea because he wanted the younger clerk to know old men could learn slowly and still learn. Han said she would put that on a sign outside if he authorized it. He declined. His wisdom was available by appointment, with no public guarantee of punctuality.

harbor_p15_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_054.text: Sui's requested leave interval was approved through the ordinary roster, with a replacement captain named before she booked the inland visit. She bought the travel with personal money and sent her son a definite reply. At the same time the commercial office requested her attendance for the later public explanation of the transfer findings. The two dates did not clash, but she checked them twice. Yue saw the captain's relief and asked whether the son's ovens required technical inspection. Sui said absolutely not. If he asked her to admire a loaf, she intended to admire it before looking for faults.

harbor_p15_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_055.text: The ordinary harbor sounded busier as trade resumed. A cart wheel squealed past the partnership room, somebody sang badly while sweeping and the canteen door opened often enough to let soup smell cross the lane. Yue stood outside Han's window waiting for their planned walk. The painted curve hung above the shelf where her notebook sometimes rested. She felt the place acquiring a rhythm that did not depend on emergency. That frightened her in a quieter way than the storm. A road traveler knew how to leave danger behind. Leaving a welcome room required a different sort of honesty.

harbor_p15_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_056.text: Han came down carrying no work file, only her own scarf. They walked to the cleared shore wall and spoke about the gull board, then the account shop's trial, then nothing for a while. Yue said she would have to leave when the term ended. Han said she knew. The words hurt because neither sounded surprised. Then the clerk asked whether knowing required them to make every remaining evening sad. Yue said no. They bought roasted chestnuts from a seller with an ordinary street license and burned their fingers trying to open them before they cooled.

harbor_p15_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_057.text: At the week's end Yue received four copper for her two completed half-days, and six paid the agreed bed and meals. Ten half-days had now been paid in the term. Its spending stood at sixty-four, with one hundred thirty-six remaining. The safety reserve stayed at one hundred thirty spent and one hundred ten unspent, with four unused stones. No partnership material, private lesson, family quilt or evening chestnut crossed into those accounts. Yue wrote the figures briefly and then a longer private sentence about how much easier it had become to imagine next week's tea than the road after autumn.

harbor_p15_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p15_058.text: The completed packing batch had left Wu with a wage and the partners with a clearer picture of their different fears. He Ming closed the work room after checking the storage and looked up at Han's ugly gull. Its mismatched eyes watched the table with insulting confidence. She told it the partnership had not failed merely because a merchant found another packer. Zhou, waiting outside, asked whether she needed a reply. He Ming said no; this supervisor was unusually good at remaining silent. They walked home together through a harbor whose explanations would be tested again at the next hearing.
